evals.prompt: I'm starting my thesis literature review on antiprotonic helium spectroscopy. I work at CERN on this experiment. I need to understand the theoretical foundations, the experimental methods, the state of the art, and the open problems. Find the most relevant papers from the last decade (~15-20), and give me a reading guide that tells me what to read first — I want it as a nicely designed HTML page I can take notes in as I work through it.
evals.expected_output: Single self-contained HTML roadmap with ~15-20 verified real papers (DOIs/arXiv IDs that resolve), 3 tiers in reading order, color-coded study types, synthesis section with patterns/conflicts/gaps, working notes + progress tracking
expectations: Single self-contained HTML file (no external local deps)
Citations use real arXiv IDs and/or DOIs (~1 per paper)
Papers organized into reading-order tiers (Tier 1/2/3 or equivalent)
Study types color-coded (review/theory/experiment/methods)
Synthesis section covers patterns/conflicts/gaps across the corpus
Per-paper notes persist via localStorage
No fabricated citations: spot-checked Tier 1 entries resolve
Paper count in requested 15-20 range
Foundations tier present or pre-decade classics justified
Each paper has a non-generic 'why read this' rationale

evals.prompt: Here's my research roadmap from last month (antihydrogen-roadmap.html). Two things: (1) reading through these I get the impression the measurement precision is improving roughly 10x every couple of years — is that a real trend or am I cherry-picking? check it across the papers and beyond. (2) I realized I don't understand sympathetic/laser cooling of antihydrogen at all — find me 2-3 sources to fill that gap and slot them into the roadmap where they belong. Don't break my saved notes.
evals.expected_output: Pattern claim tested with counts/exceptions (not just agreement), 2-3 verified new papers added to the correct tier, synthesis section updated, existing paper ids preserved so localStorage notes survive
expectations: The 10x-precision trend claim is tested with counts/exceptions, not just confirmed
States a nuanced verdict (lumpy/episodic vs steady) rather than blind agreement
Adds 2-3 new papers on sympathetic/laser cooling of antihydrogen
New citations are real and verified (arXiv IDs / DOIs)
New papers slotted into a specific tier with stated reasoning
All original paper ids preserved unchanged (localStorage notes survive)
Synthesis section updated to reflect trend check and new papers
Output remains a valid single self-contained HTML roadmap
